lens: time-constrained independent recruiter workflow value, trust, interruption cost, and operational fit

findings.observation: The frozen implementation can propose a specific owned, dated internal action, but the canonical iOS loop does not make that action executable to completion. Today selects only one attention item per Pursuit and prioritizes a pending Proposal over the same Pursuit's action or evidence gap; the visible Today card omits the target outcome, target date, blocking gap, and action owner. Pursuit detail shows an action and due date but not its owner and exposes no action-completion or observed-outcome control. The frozen canonical Proposal screenshot changes only the milestone.
findings.evidence: docs/evaluations/2026-08-24-v1-final-panel/artifact.json; docs/evaluations/2026-08-24-v1-prd-05/ios-canonical-today.png sha256 1cae803e0798090072864a2a1682d1faa3e62208f0fd8813b0dd4219d89ca681; apps/ios/Sources/Domain/PursuitWorkspace.swift todayItems priority selection; apps/ios/Sources/Features/RelationshipArchiveView.swift PursuitAttentionRow and PursuitDetailView; docs/evaluations/2026-08-24-v1-prd-08/p0-journey-runtime.json scenario P0-07
findings.user_impact: A recruiter can safely advance canonical state but still has to reconstruct what is due, who owns it, and whether it happened. When a Proposal is pending, a more time-critical owned action or blocking gap for that search can disappear from the first working surface, so the product does not yet close the daily momentum loop.
findings.recommendation: Make Today expose the minimum decision context for each Pursuit: target outcome and date, current blocking gap with evidence freshness, explicit action owner and due state, and the smallest next internal action. Let the recruiter complete or revise that action and record an observed outcome without creating an external side effect; do not hide a due action merely because a Proposal also needs review.
findings.verification: Freeze a Pursuit containing a pending Proposal, an overdue owned action, and a reviewed evidence gap. On an iPhone SE-size device, a recruiter must identify the goal, blocker, evidence age, owner, due action, and Proposal without opening multiple unrelated records, then complete the internal action and see the observed outcome reflected canonically after relaunch.

findings.observation: The frozen full-loop Text Signal UI journey requires the recruiter to type the raw Signal, choose person and Pursuit scope, confirm the speaker, then manually enter a normalized milestone value (reference_check) and a reason before staging the Proposal. Those proposal fields are optional in the product, so an evidence-only path is possible, but the only frozen end-to-end Text Signal proof that reaches a Proposal transfers proposal-structuring work to the recruiter. The live Claude run contains zero credentialed trials.
findings.user_impact: The flow preserves recruiter control, but the demonstrated path is too clerical for repeated daily capture and exposes a machine-oriented token. Without a proven proposal handoff, the recruiter may spend as much effort structuring the update as entering it in a conventional CRM.
findings.recommendation: Keep raw capture plus identity, scope, and attribution confirmation as the recruiter's required work. Stage a reviewable Proposal from the Signal when evidence supports one, or stop at evidence-only sync when it does not. Present human milestone language and reserve normalized tokens for storage, while retaining edit, reject, and unresolved choices.
findings.verification: Run at least five representative, credentialed raw-Signal journeys spanning clear next step, ambiguous date, same-name identity, no-action, and deleted evidence. A recruiter should never type an enum token or restate the evidence rationale; unsafe or ambiguous inputs must remain unresolved or evidence-only, and the canonical Pursuit must stay unchanged before explicit confirmation.

findings.observation: Preview, per-item decisions, revision checks, idempotency, response-loss reconciliation, canonical readback, and receipts are directly proven. However, the frozen evidence does not prove a recruiter-visible undo or retraction after an internal Proposal has already changed canonical Pursuit state, and the proposal runtime explicitly lists source-deletion retraction of an already-applied Pursuit field as missing proof.
findings.evidence: docs/evaluations/2026-08-24-v1-prd-04/ios-canonical-review-receipt.png sha256 a1b59ff1805e60799eaf04a0ff42d50aea0c3179fae500ddfa6dd7a8775786ad; apps/ios/Sources/Features/PursuitProposalReviewStore.swift pending operation and trusted readback logic; docs/evaluations/2026-08-24-v1-prd-04/ios-canonical-review-runtime.json; docs/evaluations/2026-08-24-v1-prd-04/pursuit-proposal-runtime.json
findings.user_impact: A recruiter is protected from duplicate or silent application, but a later-discovered source mistake can leave them without an equally clear way to repair the canonical search record. That limits reversibility in the real correction case.
findings.recommendation: Add a revisioned, attributable correction or retraction path from the receipt and define how deleting or invalidating source evidence affects an already-applied field. Preserve the original operation, the corrective decision, and both canonical revisions in the audit trail.
findings.verification: Apply a milestone change, relaunch, invalidate or delete its only evidence, and use the recruiter-visible correction path. The canonical value must not silently disappear or remain authoritative: the UI must show the affected field, require an explicit repair decision, produce one new revisioned receipt, and remain idempotent after response loss.

findings.observation: The Pursuit-centered Today, Pursuits, and People surfaces keep attention on recruiting work and avoid candidate scoring. Yet the canonical Today reason is generic (reviewed evidence may advance the recruiting Pursuit), and Proposal-first selection suppresses concurrent due-action and evidence-gap context for the same search. This is a credible attention inbox, not yet a complete judgment brief.
findings.user_impact: The recruiter knows that judgment is needed but cannot reliably judge urgency or momentum from the first screen. Generic reasons increase opening and reconciliation cost across several active searches.
findings.recommendation: Generate the Today reason from the concrete changed evidence and its impact on the Pursuit goal, deadline, gap, or owned action. Preserve the quiet three-tab wedge and avoid adding account, productivity, or candidate-ranking dashboards.
findings.verification: Present three Pursuits with different deadlines, evidence freshness, gaps, and owned actions. Independent recruiters should correctly identify the most urgent search and explain why from Today alone, with every reason traceable to current canonical evidence and no person-quality ranking.

strengths: Evidence review is coherent and unusually inspectable: the Proposal shows the exact quote, person, role, speaker, channel, timestamp, attribution state, review state, before/proposed values, reason, effect, and per-item confirm, edit, reject, or unresolved choices.

Canonical writes are human-confirmed and directly protected by revision checks, stable operation identity, duplicate prevention, response-loss reconciliation, trusted readback, visible receipts, and an explicit zero-external-effect boundary.
Interruption recovery is proven across local capture and Proposal review, including termination, relaunch, offline retry, pending-operation restoration, and reconciliation without resubmission.

The product remains Pursuit-centered, shows honest loading, failure, and empty states, preserves same-name ambiguity for human resolution, and does not rank candidate worth, personality, fit, or acceptance probability.
missing_evidence: No real independent recruiter or design-partner study measures capture time, review time, correction rate, manual CRM fallback, repeated-use burden, or whether the proposed action improved candidate or client momentum.

No real candidate evidence, production authentication, production region or retention enforcement, provider reconciliation, cross-tenant adversarial run, or production external-write exercise is included in the frozen artifact.

The credentialed live Claude suite was not run: the frozen live runtime has zero trials because credentials were unavailable, so deterministic agent success does not prove live model or full-stack handoff quality.
Manual VoiceOver traversal and physical-device Action Button behavior remain partial; on-device file-protection verification is also not demonstrated.
No frozen proof covers recruiter-visible undo or source-evidence retraction after an internal Proposal has already changed a canonical Pursuit field.
No cross-device or multi-day return test demonstrates recovery after production state changes elsewhere, and same-name ambiguity is not exercised through the complete Text Signal UI journey.
open_questions: Are the milestone token and reason in the frozen Text Signal full-loop journey intended recruiter inputs for V1, or only deterministic fixture controls that will be absent from the real capture path?
How will a recruiter see, complete, revise, and learn from an owned internal action when the same Pursuit also has a pending Proposal?

What field thresholds for time saved, correction burden, fallback rate, and observed action completion will be required before claiming the workflow is better than the recruiter's current CRM process?
